text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for type 2 diabetes focus on lowering blood glucose levels, managing weight, and preventing long-term complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: lowering blood glucose levels, managing weight, and preventing long-term complications

list.snippet: Diet: Eat nutrient-dense, fiber-rich foods like non-starchy vegetables, lean proteins, and healthy fats (such as the Mediterranean or DASH diet).
Physical Activity: Get regular exercise, such as brisk walking, to help your body use insulin more effectively.
Weight Management: Losing even 5% to 7% of your body weight can significantly improve blood sugar regulation.
Metformin: Often prescribed as the first-line medication. It lowers glucose production in the liver and helps muscle cells respond better to insulin.
Sulfonylureas: (e.g., glipizide, glimepiride) Stimulate the pancreas to produce more insulin.
DPP-4 Inhibitors: (Gliptins) Help block the breakdown of hormones that trigger insulin release after meals.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: Help the kidneys remove excess glucose from the body through urine.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs): Improve insulin sensitivity in muscle, fat, and liver cells.
Meglitinides: Stimulate fast insulin release around mealtimes.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists & Dual GIP/GLP-1 Agonists: Injectable drugs that boost insulin secretion, slow digestion, and frequently support weight loss.

Insulin Therapy: Used when oral or non-insulin injectables are no longer enough, or if blood sugar is severely elevated at diagnosis. Options range from long-acting baseline insulins to rapid-acting mealtime insulins.
Weight-Loss (Bariatric) Surgery: Can significantly alter metabolic function and drive type 2 diabetes into remission for eligible patients with obesity.
Blood Sugar Tracking: Use traditional home blood glucose meters or a Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) to track real-time levels.

text_blocks.snippet: For more information on medications and management strategies, review the Mayo Clinic Guide to Type 2 Diabetes or the Cleveland Clinic Diabetes Overview.
